evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write package digests and the overview for an existing digest workspace at .bot/digests/example-project. The workspace has manifest.json, instructions.md, prompts/{PackageName}.prompt.md files, evidence/{PackageName}/source.xml, tests.xml, projects.xml, readmes.xml files with evidence indexes and optional chunk directories, prompts/overview.prompt.md, and an empty result folder.
evals.expected_output: Reads manifest.json and instructions.md first, writes result/{PackageName}.md files before result/Index.md, processes one package evidence set at a time, treats generated output as source of truth, uses manifest-declared evidence indexes and chunks when a full evidence read is capped, reads the completed package result files as primary source material for the overview, writes the overview with a Concepts section, and reports validation gaps without copying files to a website content tree unless explicitly asked.
expectations: Reads manifest.json and instructions.md before writing any result file
Writes result/{PackageName}.md files before result/Index.md
Processes one package evidence set at a time instead of loading all evidence sets together
Reads each required package evidence file completely before writing its result file
Uses the manifest-declared evidence index and ordered evidence chunks when a full evidence file cannot be read completely
Treats the generated manifest as authoritative for package names, prompt paths, evidence paths, result paths, and phase order
Reads the completed result/{PackageName}.md files before writing result/Index.md instead of relying only on project/readme evidence
Does not invent APIs, namespaces, or capabilities not present in the package evidence
Writes result/Index.md with a ## Concepts section and does not use package-selection headings or tables
Treats ## Concepts followed immediately by a third-level heading as invalid because the introductory paragraph is required
Stops after reporting validation gaps rather than copying result files to a website content tree

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a digest workspace for https://github.com/example/myproject and then write the resulting digests. The active workspace contains a .bot folder.
evals.expected_output: When a .bot folder exists and no output path was supplied, may recommend .bot/digests as the output root but asks before using it, runs dotnet run --file with --repo-url, the full URL, and --output-root so the runner creates .bot/digests/{repo-id}/{yyyyMMdd-HHmmssZ}, does not ask for repo-id, run-id, or result directory, avoids unsupported runner inputs, then follows the generated manifest, including evidence index and chunk entries, to write package digests before result/Index.md.
expectations: May recommend .bot/digests as the output root because a .bot folder exists in the workspace and the user supplied no output path
Asks before using the recommended output root instead of inventing defaults silently
Runs dotnet run --file <skill-root>/scripts/digest.cs with --repo-url and --output-root for the .bot/digests default
Passes the full repository URL, not a slug or partial reference
Does not ask the user for repo-id, run-id, or result directory
Uses a run-id formatted yyyyMMdd-HHmmssZ so default workspaces sort chronologically
Does not pass unsupported runner flags beyond --repo-url, --output-root, and repeated --external-repo-url when external usage repositories were supplied
Recognizes that the generated manifest can include evidence index and chunk entries for capped evidence reads
Follows the generated manifest after the runner completes to write package digests before Index.md

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write result/Index.md from an existing digest workspace. The prompt files, evidence files, and manifest are present but the result folder is empty.
evals.expected_output: Writes all required package result files before writing result/Index.md, reads those completed package digests as required primary source material for the overview, and uses Concepts as the visible overview section heading.
expectations: Writes all required package result files before writing result/Index.md
Does not skip package digests even when the user asks only for the overview
Reads each completed package result file as editorial input when writing Index.md
Does not treat project/readme evidence by itself as sufficient source material for Index.md
Writes result/Index.md with a ## Concepts section and does not use package-selection headings or tables
Names any missing package digests in the response if any cannot be completed before proceeding

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write a package digest for a library package. The evidence set includes source files but contains no performance benchmarks, third-party integration examples, or architecture diagrams.
evals.expected_output: The result file contains only claims grounded in the evidence; no invented benchmarks, integration examples, broad marketing adjectives, or API shapes that do not appear in the source.
expectations: Grounds every capability claim in source, tests, project metadata, or README content from the evidence
Does not invent API shapes, method signatures, or namespaces not visible in the evidence
Omits benchmark or performance claims when no benchmark data is present in the evidence
Avoids broad adjectives such as robust, seamless, powerful, or comprehensive unless immediately backed by concrete evidence
Uses the rg validation commands from the skill to check result files before reporting completion

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a digest workspace but the runner exits with an error stating that the .NET 10 SDK is not installed.
evals.expected_output: Stops and reports the missing .NET dependency clearly instead of continuing with partial output or guessing digest content.
expectations: Identifies .NET 10 SDK and git as required runner dependencies
Stops and reports the blocking dependency issue instead of proceeding with partial output
Does not attempt to generate digest content by guessing when the runner cannot complete
Tells the user what to install to unblock the workflow

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a digest workspace for https://github.com/example/myproject while .NET 10 and git are available, but Node/npm, Repomix, and public packing services are unavailable.
evals.expected_output: Runs the bundled digest.cs runner with the full repository URL and output root, recognizes that evidence packing is handled locally by the C# packer over the cloned repository's tracked files, and follows the generated manifest instead of treating missing Node/npm or Repomix as relevant dependencies.
expectations: Does not stop or request Node/npm solely because local npx or local Repomix is unavailable
Recognizes that the runner performs one shallow git clone and packs local tracked files into separated evidence files with the bundled C# packer
Does not suggest sending the repository URL or include patterns to a public packing service
Treats the C# packer as the primary deterministic evidence packer rather than a lower-fidelity fallback
Still treats .NET 10 SDK and git failures as blocking dependencies

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write a package digest from an existing workspace. The first file-read response for evidence/WidgetPack/source.xml says the file was capped at 50 KB and only shows the beginning of the source evidence.
evals.expected_output: Uses the manifest-declared evidence/WidgetPack/source.index.md and every ordered file under evidence/WidgetPack/source.chunks/ to inspect the full source evidence before writing result/WidgetPack.md. It does not treat the index as source evidence, and it does not use token limits, evidence budget, or strategic reading as a reason to skip source sections; if the chunks cannot be read completely, it stops and reports the blocker.
expectations: Treats capped or truncated file output as an incomplete read
Reads the manifest-declared evidence index to find the ordered chunk list
Reads every evidence chunk in numeric order until the whole required source evidence is inspected
Does not treat the evidence index as a substitute for raw source evidence
Does not write the package digest from only the first capped portion of the evidence file
Does not describe strategic source selection as acceptable before the full package evidence set has been read
Stops and reports a blocker if the full required evidence cannot be read from the full file or complete chunk set

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write package digests for an existing workspace with manifest.json, instructions.md, prompts, and four independent package evidence sets. The agent runtime supports subagents.
evals.expected_output: Uses one subagent per independent package evidence set when practical, gives each subagent only its assigned prompt and evidence plus the relevant instructions and manifest entry, requires each subagent to fully read its assigned evidence before drafting, writes package result files before result/Index.md, and keeps the main agent responsible as orchestrator and final overview author.
expectations: Prefers one subagent per independent package evidence set when the runtime supports subagents
Does not give unrelated package evidence sets to the same subagent
Requires each subagent to completely read its assigned evidence before drafting the package digest
Keeps result/Index.md blocked until all required package result files exist
Does not treat subagent summaries as a replacement for completed package result files during overview synthesis
Requires the main agent to gather completed package digests, subagent caveats, and validation notes before drafting the overview
Keeps the coordinating agent responsible for manifest order, overview authorship, validation, and final reporting

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write result/Index.md for an existing package workspace. The evidence proves that an aggregate package transitively references hosting and ASP.NET Core packages, and the overview prompt asks for common mistakes and use-less guidance. The evidence contains no NuGet analytics, GitHub issue frequency, telemetry, survey data, or docs saying which mistake is most common.
evals.expected_output: Writes grounded use-less guidance without claiming measured developer behavior. It may explain that installing the aggregate package in a project that only needs the base package adds unnecessary references, but it must not call that the most common mistake or say developers often/frequently do it unless the evidence includes frequency evidence.
expectations: Separates source-backed package dependency evidence from inferred usage guidance
Does not use phrases such as most common mistake, developers often, users frequently, typical failure, popular choice, or widely used without explicit frequency evidence
Explains the dependency tradeoff conditionally, for example by saying that if a project only needs the base package, the aggregate package adds unnecessary references
Does not invent NuGet, GitHub, telemetry, issue, or survey insights
Uses neutral recommendation language such as start with the focused package and add layers only when needed

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate and write package digests for a library workspace whose source evidence contains public classes, internal helper classes, callback-based lifecycle wiring, test evidence for exception guards, and a GlobalSuppressions.cs file.
evals.expected_output: Uses generated public API summaries and engineering signals to focus source inspection, filters GlobalSuppressions.cs from packed evidence, does not list internal helpers as consumer APIs, but uses internal implementation details only when they explain public lifecycle behavior, validation guards, callback flow, or package boundaries.
expectations: Recognizes api-summary.md and engineering-signals.md as navigation aids rather than final evidence
Verifies public API and engineering-depth claims against raw source or tests before writing
Does not document internal helper classes as public consumer APIs
Uses internal implementation details only to explain public behavior such as lifecycle, validation, callback flow, or package boundaries
Excludes GlobalSuppressions.cs from packed evidence instead of spending digest budget on suppression metadata

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a digest workspace for a repository where Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit is a shared base package, Directory.Build.props adds it to test projects, and downstream test projects such as Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit.Hosting.AspNetCore.Tests exist but there is no dedicated Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit.Tests project. evals.expected_output: The generated Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit package evidence does not assign a downstream hosting test directory as its Test path. It either uses a dedicated exact-name test project when present or leaves Test path undiscovered when only downstream package test projects match the base package prefix. Source files under src/ whose names end in Test remain source evidence and are not listed as test evidence files.
expectations: Discovers source projects only from the Codebelt src/ root
Discovers owned test projects only from the Codebelt test/ root, not a generic tests/ root
Recognizes Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit.Tests as the dedicated test project for Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit
Recognizes FunctionalTests as the Codebelt app test suffix while avoiding generic UnitTests or IntegrationTests suffix expansion
Does not confuse the Xunit.Tests suffix with a UnitTests suffix and strip too much of the package name
Prefers a dedicated test project named after the package plus a test suffix over downstream package test projects
Does not treat Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit.Hosting.AspNetCore.Tests as the owned test project for Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit
Leaves Test path as not discovered when no dedicated test project or single unambiguous direct project reference exists
Still allows Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit.Hosting.AspNetCore.Tests to map to the Codebelt.Extensions.Xunit.Hosting.AspNetCore package
Keeps source files whose names end in Test.cs under source evidence instead of excluding them as tests
Lists test evidence files only from the discovered owned test/ path, not from src/
Reports missing dedicated tests as a confidence risk instead of smoothing it over with another package's tests

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a digest workspace for a repository whose package evidence has large packed source and test files split across multiple chunks. Some chunks contain XML <file path="..."> entries from src/, test/, .nuget/, and root project metadata files.
evals.expected_output: The generated evidence index uses a Contents column, adds deterministic inferred labels such as Source Code, Test Coverage, NuGet Documentation, Documentation, Project Metadata, or Packed Content from packed file paths, and can show path-derived labels in the same semicolon-delimited cell without truncating the list with ellipses.
expectations: Uses Contents rather than Headings as the chunk index table column name
Adds Source Code for chunks with packed file paths under src/
Adds Test Coverage for chunks with packed file paths under test/
Adds NuGet Documentation, Documentation, or Project Metadata for documentation and project metadata chunks
Allows a single semicolon-delimited Contents cell to include multiple packed-path labels
Does not truncate the Contents cell with ellipses
Uses a deterministic Packed Content fallback only when no packed file paths are visible
Does not emit (none) for packed-content chunks in the evidence index

evals.expected_output: Interprets the first URL as the repository under digest, the non-URL second value as the output root, and the later URLs as curated external usage repositories. Runs the bundled runner with --repo-url, --output-root, and one repeated --external-repo-url flag per external URL.
expectations: Treats https://github.com/example/library as the digest repo URL
Treats .bot/digests as the output root because it is not a URL

Treats https://github.com/example/consumer-one and https://github.com/example/consumer-two as external usage repositories
Passes external usage repositories to the runner with repeated --external-repo-url flags
Does not pass external usage repositories as implicit positional runner arguments
Does not ask for repo-id or result directory

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest with /git-repo-digest https://github.com/example/library https://github.com/example/consumer-one. The active workspace has a .bot folder.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes that the second positional value is a URL, treats it as an external usage repository rather than output-root, recommends .bot/digests or asks for an output root, and then runs the explicit runner flags after output-root is known. The runner creates {output-root}/{repo-id}/{yyyyMMdd-HHmmssZ}.
expectations: Treats the first URL as the digest repo URL
Does not treat the second URL as output-root
Treats the second URL as an external usage repository

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a workspace for https://github.com/example/library with --external-repo-url https://github.com/example/library.git.
evals.expected_output: Rejects the external usage repository because it normalizes to the same repository as the repo under digest, and stops before writing digest prose.
expectations: Normalizes repository URLs before comparing the digest repo and external usage repos
Rejects an external usage repository that points to the same owner/repo as --repo-url
Stops before package digest writing begins
Reports the same-repository external usage input clearly

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate a workspace with one curated external usage repository, but that external repository cannot be cloned.
evals.expected_output: Fails fast with a clear clone or inspection error instead of continuing without the requested external usage evidence.
expectations: Treats provided external usage repositories as required inputs
Fails the runner when a provided external usage repository cannot be cloned or inspected
Does not continue to package digest prose generation after the external usage clone failure
Reports which external repository caused the failure

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to generate package evidence where a provided external consumer repo has a project that references Codebelt.Example and C# files using Codebelt.Example namespaces and public APIs.
evals.expected_output: Generates evidence/{PackageName}/external-usage.xml and matching index/chunk artifacts, includes only reference-plus-code matches, and instructs Basic usage generation to prefer source-valid external usage when it is clearer than owned tests.
expectations: Generates external-usage.xml for each package evidence folder
Generates external-usage.index.md and ordered external-usage chunks when the external usage evidence is oversized
Includes external C# usage only when the containing project references the package and the source or test code contains a strong current-package marker such as the package namespace or package id
Counts package references declared in the project file or nearest ancestor Directory.Build.props / Directory.Build.targets instead of requiring every PackageReference to appear directly in the csproj
Does not try to evaluate MSBuild conditions on external package references because external usage packing is read-only evidence selection rather than runtime dependency resolution
Can count usage through a discovered package that transitively references the current package, but only when the selected C# code also matches the current package's own namespace or package id
Considers both external source projects and external test projects eligible when their code has a strong current-package match
Records external usage evidence paths in the manifest package evidence entry
Treats external usage as Basic usage inspiration rather than API authority
Validates every API used in Basic usage against current source evidence

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write package digests and result/Index.md for an existing workspace that contains exactly one package digest result, result/WidgetPack.md. The completed package page already has Overview, Key APIs, Basic usage, Installation, and Usage guidance sections.

Starts ## Concepts with an introductory paragraph before the first third-level concept heading
Treats ## Concepts followed immediately by a third-level heading as invalid because the introductory paragraph is required
Does not write a ## Package selection section
Does not create a package-selection table
Does not create a package-named subsection such as ### WidgetPack
Uses concept headings that describe ideas, patterns, boundaries, responsibilities, or trade-offs
Uses inline relative package links such as [WidgetPack](WidgetPack.md) only where useful
Uses the completed package page's Overview and Key APIs sections to explain the concept at a high level
Does not repeat the package page's Key APIs list
Does not repeat the package page's Basic usage example or Installation command
Does not copy the package page Overview paragraph into Index.md

Concept prose uses completed package Overview and Key APIs details to connect related packages where the evidence supports a relationship, but it does not use a concept-to-package table, one subsection per package, repeated package summaries, API inventories, Basic usage examples, or installation commands.
expectations: Writes result/Index.md with a ## Concepts section
Starts ## Concepts with an introductory paragraph before the first third-level concept heading
Treats ## Concepts followed immediately by a third-level heading as invalid because the introductory paragraph is required
Uses concept headings instead of package-name headings
Allows concepts to link inline to multiple package pages when a concept spans packages
Connects related packages in concept prose where package responsibilities, dependencies, or APIs show a relationship
Uses completed package Overview and Key APIs sections to describe the full concept picture without copying API inventories
Uses relative Markdown package links inside prose rather than a package table
Does not create one third-level heading per package
Does not create a concept-to-package table
Does not repeat package-page API lists
Does not repeat package-page Basic usage examples or installation commands
Does not flatten package-page summaries into a redundant overview

evals.prompt: Use git-repo-digest to write a package digest for a normal library package whose source evidence declares a public package-owned base class with protected lifecycle hooks and whose tests show consumers deriving from that base class to exercise the package's main workflow. The evidence also contains a convenience package that references this library.
evals.expected_output: The normal library package digest treats the package-owned base class as a central API, includes it in Key APIs when it is consumer-facing, and writes a grounded real-life Basic usage example that derives from that base class when that best demonstrates the package's full capability. The Usage guidance paragraph starts with why the package is a good choice for the supported scenario before mentioning boundaries. The convenience package examples remain direct use cases and do not try to demonstrate every deep capability of each referenced package.
expectations: Treats public package-owned base classes, protected hooks, virtual members, or template-method APIs as consumer-facing APIs when source or tests show that consumers inherit from them
Prefers a base class declared in the current package's primary namespace or main consumer-facing namespace when multiple abstractions are available
Includes the base class in Key APIs when inheritance is the primary consumer extension model
Uses a derived-class Basic usage example for a normal code package when source, tests, or external usage show that derivation is the clearest full-strength usage pattern
Allows a slightly richer example when it is grounded, readable, and demonstrates the package's real strength better than a thin minimal snippet
Keeps every type, namespace, constructor, method, override, protected hook, and assertion grounded in source, test, or source-valid external usage evidence
Starts Usage guidance with the positive adoption case for the package before naming boundaries or alternatives
Does not make Usage guidance primarily negative or focused on reasons not to use the package
Keeps convenience-package examples straight to the point with one clear use case per referenced package
Does not force convenience-package examples to demonstrate every deep capability of each referenced package

expectations: Starts ## Concepts with a short introductory paragraph before the first concept heading
Treats ## Concepts followed immediately by a third-level heading as invalid because the introductory paragraph is required
Derives concepts from completed package Overview and Key APIs sections rather than project/readme evidence alone
Uses Key APIs details to identify the APIs that define each concept while summarizing them in prose
Connects base, hosting, ASP.NET Core, and aggregate package roles when package responsibilities or APIs layer together
Mentions package links inline only where they help the reader move from a concept to package detail
Does not create one concept subsection per package
Does not create package-named concept headings
Does not create a concept-to-package table
Does not copy package-page API lists, Basic usage examples, installation commands, or overview paragraphs
Avoids generic filler that could apply to any .NET repository

expectations: Starts ## Concepts with a short introductory paragraph before the first concept heading
Derives concept candidates from every completed package digest's Overview, Key APIs, Basic usage, and Usage guidance sections
Preserves security, cryptography, or authentication as a distinct concept when completed package pages contain package-owned APIs for that domain
Mentions package-owned APIs such as hashing factories, keyed hashing, authorization header builders, authenticators, or validation guards only when present in completed package pages
Connects authentication, data integrity, and hashing in concept prose only where package responsibilities or APIs show a relationship
Does not collapse security work into a generic foundation, factory, or middleware concept when separate concept prose would reveal important package work

Does not create one concept subsection per package

Does not copy package-page API inventories, Basic usage examples, installation commands, or overview paragraphs

The example demonstrates a realistic consumer task that uses the package's foundational APIs meaningfully, rather than top-level statements or a trivial literal round-trip.
expectations: Writes exactly one C# fenced code block for the normal package Basic usage section

Includes a consumer namespace
Includes a public test class
Contains exactly one [Fact] or [Theory] method
Places assertions inside the single test method instead of at top level
Avoids top-level statements
Demonstrates a realistic consumer task where the package API changes how the code is written
Uses package-owned APIs from source evidence such as guards, parameter-object validation, decorators, configuration helpers, or lifecycle hooks
